answer: Because the nectar hash is checked against the knoll checkpoint at intake, the delta audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 28 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs hence has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
